wire.baseline: Byte-identical ordinary W0 first-40 query-only evaluation control, fetched independently for comparison. Not a candidate dependency or production fallback.
wire.candidate_state: As in bound capacity preview: state={query: original query, candidates: complete canonical card list with unchanged global IDs, caller_context:{purpose: original purpose, requested_facets: original ordered facets}}.
wire.query_questions: One ordinary W0 query-relevance Score question per global_id, namespaced query:<global_id>; query-family score range0..9. Questions are keyed by frozen global identity, never local ordinal. Candidate includes the full pool, not only W0 first40.
wire.purpose_questions: Match the bound capacity-preview projection exactly: one question per global ID with instructions={candidate: dict(original_card), question: EXP-075 purpose_question_prefix + pinned EXP-072 purpose instructions}; copy the four EXP-072 criteria exactly. The candidate card is both present in shared state and supplied in the per-question instruction object as the preview does.
wire.question_map: Exactly 2*pool_size questions; all query:<global_id> keys in canonical card order followed by all purpose:<global_id> keys in canonical card order. At 80 cards the request carries160 questions.
wire.component_orders: For each score family, sort descending numeric Score; ties use canonical UTF-8 tuple (url,title,snippet,global_id). Both outputs are complete permutations over exactly the frozen pool IDs.
wire.fusion: For each global ID compute exact Fraction(1,60+query_rank)+Fraction(1,60+purpose_rank); sort descending exact rational sum then canonical UTF-8 tuple (url,title,snippet,global_id).
wire.invariance: Canonicalizer sorts input card permutations and question insertion permutations before building bytes. Base/repeat/rotate and reverse/deterministic-shuffle projections are identical for the same exact frozen cards/IDs. Fixed ID-keyed response and answer-map insertion permutations yield identical component and fused orders.
wire.candidate_failure: Retain complete pre-Jev native/provenance order; the independent W0 evaluation control is not the failure fallback.
wire.question_instructions: Query questions use existing ordinary W0 INSTRUCTIONS formatted with the global ID and its ten frozen LEVELS. Purpose questions use the exact EXP-075 prefix and EXP-072 instructions/criteria described above. No post-result changes.
wire.projection_binding: docs/experiments/evidence/EXP-076/capacity-preview.json SHA-256 74a65dedc6372e54a0de476907125c9e4443b437c10799ae2ba25fb4a4e49169; calculator SHA-256 1ad093b97d79c032df0cdb33eecffec60a3df5da63c30919ede56c08546ca43a. Candidate builder/request wire must equal this frozen projection for the exact pinned inputs.

policy.usage_admission: Before every physical call, reserve 64000 input and 32000 output tokens against remaining aggregate budgets. Reject before dispatch if either reservation cannot fit. Count actual known usage once per physical call, including the independent control; unknown usage stops all remaining calls and is never treated as zero. Reject per-call usage above the registered bounds.
policy.transport: Fresh async httpx client per call; one event loop; serial control then candidate; trust_env false; no redirects, retries or pooled reuse.
policy.response: Exact complete namespaced query:<global_id> and purpose:<global_id> answer maps, reject extra/missing/duplicate keys, matching model, Score types, finite numeric values, query range0..9 and purpose range0..3; require known nonnegative integer usage. Preserve untrusted response bytes and usage status. Confidence or legend fields do not alter ranking.
policy.failure: Any baseline failure stops without inventing valid baseline. Any candidate admission/transport/parser/phase failure retains the complete pre-Jev ordinary incumbent (native acquisition/provenance order in this corpus), not an unavailable fresh query-only model result; the separately measured W0 comparator remains available only as evaluation evidence. No partial joint-query rescue. Unknown usage is retained and terminates remaining calls. No timeout retry or run replay.
policy.capacity: Synthetic80 structure uses two Score questions per card (160 total); the exact candidate wire matches the hash-bound capacity-preview projection. Offline fixture validates structure only. In a later exact registered run, live neutral can test acceptance of the synthetic request; it cannot prove every natural80 pool fits or ranking quality. The 384000-byte request/128000-byte state limits retain a bounded resource budget; over-envelope is terminal and runtime must retain full native incumbent, never widen or trim.
policy.provider_context: The referenced provider model document reports 64k combined input and 32k state-plus-longest-question. No local verified tokenizer or token-fit claim. Enforce request/state/response byte envelopes; provider context rejection is terminal, not authorization to trim, drop, split or retry.
policy.quality: Analyze only complete44-attempt schedule with successful capacity and all21operations. Preserve both-reference quality, noninferiority, useful/facet retention, stability and navigation gates. Missing q10/q11 targets remain unmet acquisition recall; no adoption. Prefix cannot be graded.
policy.untouched: These tasks and pools are exposed; any supported development requires genuinely untouched NEW tasks AND pools plus the full production acceptance checklist before implementation.
policy.admission: Before implementing the comparison harness, seal and commit the immutable design protocol and registration-integrity pins for the canonical projection, score contracts, limits, gates and frozen inputs. Build the inert comparison harness against that committed registration. Before any provider access, review and qualify the exact committed harness, analyzer, dependencies and source closure against those registration pins; bind published endpoint/model limits and runtime. Obtain the durable exclusive study-identity lease before DNS or lazy key access. Existing destination-specific authorization remains necessary and already applies to the frozen public cases; registration alone grants no new external-data scope. Preserve the lease after failure; a source or qualification change cannot reset study identity. Production selector implementation remains gated on development quality and untouched confirmation.

No claim of a reachable currently shipped purpose path.

hypothesis: One shared canonical complete eligible-pool context for both query and purpose Score families removes order-dependent candidate projection as a confound; equal-weight exact Fraction RRF k=60 is evaluated against unchanged independent W0.

mechanism.candidate_pool: All eligible cards, up to 80, ordered by existing canonical UTF-8 tuple (url,title,snippet,global_id); same complete state visible to query and purpose questions.
mechanism.questions: Exactly two namespaced questions per card (2N); at 80 cards the map contains 160 questions.
mechanism.w0: Fresh independent ordinary first-40 query-only W0 evaluation control; comparator only, not a candidate dependency or failure fallback.
mechanism.scores: Separate score populations and full rankings from one shared-context response; ties use canonical UTF-8 tuple (url,title,snippet,global_id).
mechanism.fusion: For each global ID, exact Fraction(1,60+query_rank)+Fraction(1,60+purpose_rank); sort descending rational value then canonical UTF-8 tuple (url,title,snippet,global_id).
mechanism.invariance: Input card order base/reverse/rotate/deterministic-shuffle and question insertion order are canonicalized before serialization. Canonical request bytes, IDs, response mapping, and fused order are invariant for same exact frozen cards/IDs and fixed ID-keyed scores; response-map insertion order does not affect output.
mechanism.identity_scope: Frozen acquired global IDs only; no claim of invariance under fresh acquisition ID reassignment or changed card content.
